| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | *(pending)* |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Historically-grounded philosophical and systematic theology scholarship engaging Thomas Aquinas and the Thomistic tradition, plus dialogue between Thomism and modern philosophy/theology. Confirmed from actual 2025-2026 tables of contents: natural law theory and its historical sources (Aquinas and Maimonides), philosophy of God/first principles, analogy of being/scholastic metaphysics (John of St. Thomas), political theology (Church-state relations, Maritain), race/equity examined through a Thomistic-Augustinian lens, historical theology (Augustine on original sin), liturgical theology, prayer and spirituality in Aquinas. All confirmed articles are text-based scholarly/historical-philosophical argumentation; none are empirical, quantitative, or social-science methods.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** historical-textual/exegetical analysis of Aquinas and Thomistic commentators, systematic theology, analytic and scholastic metaphysics, philosophy of religion / natural theology, history of philosophy (medieval, patristic, early modern reception of Aquinas), political philosophy/theology in the Thomistic tradition, review essays and book reviews

- **experiential.review_time_months**: SciRev has no entry for this journal (confirmed via direct site search and Google site: search -- 0 results); no Reddit r/AskAcademia threads found; no Chinese-language (小木虫/知乎/fabiaoji) discussion found. Only source is a ~1980s print guidebook, too stale to report as current.
- **experiential.desk_reject_pct**: Same as above -- only a ~1980s figure (~1% of submissions sent to external review) exists; no current source.
- **experiential.reviewer_culture**: No first-hand author accounts in English or Chinese-language forums describing reviewer tone/culture were found for this niche Catholic Thomistic philosophy/theology journal.
